question: The header's Sources field names hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.md (Success, Team and delivery, Demo accounts) and hsdd/context/update-1-add-phone.md (Change: AC-2.1 amended, AC-2.4; Demo accounts), both superseded by PRD v2 (Q-046, Q-050). How does the citation touch move them, and does the moved entry also gain the PRD v2 sections the node's own text now cites?

options.label: one PRD v2 entry matching the root's copy
options.consequence: The header reads (Success, Team and delivery, Constraints, Demo accounts, AC-2.1, AC-2.4), byte for byte the embedded copy S12 wrote (DEC-107, DEC-108), so H19's ripple has nothing to settle. The field still lacks AC-2.3, AC-4.4, AC-5.5 and AC-6.2, which the Overview cites, until H18 adds them.

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, headings only
options.consequence: Each PRD 1 heading moves to the PRD v2 heading of the same name (Success, Team and delivery, Demo accounts, AC-2.1, AC-2.4) and Constraints is left out; the header then differs from the embedded copy, and PRD 1's laptop-only line, which PRD v2 moved to Constraints, loses its pointer.

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, plus the newly cited sections
options.consequence: The field is complete now, but the touch adds citations rather than moving them, and the header differs from the embedded copy, which this step cannot write, until H19.

chosen: one PRD v2 entry matching the root's copy
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch moves a node's Sources entry for a source document to the current version and changes only citations. PRD v2's header supersedes prd-simple-login.md together with update-1-add-phone.md, so one entry replaces both. PRD 1's Success, Team and delivery and Demo accounts have PRD v2 sections of the same names; PRD 1 Team and delivery's 'Local demo only for now: both run on a developer laptop' is PRD v2 Constraints' 'Local laptop only, as before', so a move that keeps what the citation pointed at names Constraints too (DEC-108), and the node's own Isolation strategy and Overview already cite PRD v2 Constraints. Update 1's Change (AC-2.1 amended, AC-2.4) is PRD v2 AC-2.1 and AC-2.4 inside US-2, and its Demo accounts merged into PRD v2 Demo accounts. The union is the embedded copy's list, the mapping S13 and S14 used for their headers (DEC-117, DEC-122). The intake record's Sources and Scope paragraph gives newly governing sections to each phase-plan-append, so they go to H18 as a consider. Had PRD v2 Team and delivery kept the laptop line, the headings-only move would have led.

question: The file cites profile-api@v1 six times: the header's Consumes line, simple-login.integration.1's Consumes and its Scope ('which profile-api@v1 guarantees answers like an expired one'), and simple-login.integration.2's Scope (the v1 fixture path the replay moved from; 'comments that cite profile-api@v1 move to v2') and Dependencies ('integration.1's replay of profile-api@v1's exact 200 fixtures'). profile-api@v1 is stable, not deprecated, coexisting with v2. What does the touch do with them, and where does the one consider item go?

options.label: leave all six; one consider to simple-login.integration
options.consequence: The integration node's next planning (H18) and its reconcile (H19) see one item naming profile-api@v2: the appended phases consume v2, not v1, and the ripple keeps v1 in Consumes while integration.1 names it.

options.label: leave all six; consider to simple-login.backend
options.consequence: Joins Q-056 at the producer, but the citing phases are this consumer's, and only this node's planning decides what its new phases consume.

options.label: move the header's Consumes to profile-api@v2 only
options.consequence: Moves a contract version in a node header's Consumes line, which the citation-touch rule forbids; hsdd-reconcile's ripple writes it, keeping every version the node's phases name.

chosen: leave all six; one consider to simple-login.integration
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch: an earlier version that is neither deprecated nor retired stays live beside the new one, so every citation of it is left, and one consider item naming the new version goes to the node whose plan would move to it, the node of the citing phase. Every citing phase here is simple-login.integration's, and both are shipped (verification docs for simple-login.integration.1 and .2 on main), so five of the six are history; the sixth is the Consumes line, which is reconcile's in any case. No live sentence outside the phases cites v1: the Overview and Isolation strategy name auth-api@v1, booking-api@v1 and ADR-001 only. S13 and S14 routed the same item to their own node (DEC-118, DEC-124). An unshipped integration phase still planned on v1 would have made that phase's handoff the target instead.

question: Outside the two shipped phase sections, the Phase Plan carries the dated paragraph 'Update 1 (2026-10-30, hsdd/management/2026-10-30-intake-add-phone.md) appends simple-login.integration.2 ...' with its two bullets, and it ends 'Both ids are the provisional ones in profile-api@v2's front matter', while profile-api@v2's front matter now reads phase_ids: final. Is the paragraph history, or live text whose Update 1 citation moves and whose last sentence is restated?

options.label: history: keep it whole
options.consequence: The paragraph keeps Update 1 and 'provisional', both true of 2026-10-30, the day it records; a reader learns the ids' current standing from profile-api@v2's front matter, which names the same two ids.

options.label: live: move Update 1 to PRD v2 and restate 'provisional' as 'final'
options.consequence: The paragraph would claim PRD v2 appended integration.2, which is false, and the edit rewrites an account of what the 2026-10-30 append did.

why: hsdd-spec's citation touch keeps the version historical text describes, a dated amendment entry among them. The paragraph opens with its date and intake record and says what that append did: integration.2 appended under the same policy, sized and tiered as its bullets say, with the ids profile-api@v2 then carried as provisional. Every clause is a statement about 2026-10-30, and the phase it introduces is shipped. The ids it names are still the ones in profile-api@v2's front matter (produced_by simple-login.backend.3, consumers simple-login.web.4 and simple-login.integration.2), so nothing in it misleads about which phases they are. The preamble above it ('The node is one composition phase, so the policy only fixes its place') cites hsdd/conventions.md, whose Ordering policy is still interfaces-first, and is the 2026-10-29 plan that the dated paragraph amends; it names no superseded version and is left. An undated sentence stating the ids are provisional now would have been restated.

question: Q-039 to Q-045 target H18, simple-login.integration's phase-plan-append, and reached this citation touch only because H18's target is the same node (B-10); the step must close every routed item, and a closed item no longer reaches H18. How are they closed?

options.label: close each as explained and carry its text to H18
options.consequence: H18 receives every item whole with the same kind; the queue gains seven new ids, the churn DEC-087 already logged as an hsdd-auto defect.

options.label: close each as addressed
options.consequence: Claims work this step did not do: a citation touch changes only citations, and every item is Phase Plan content; H18 would never see them.

chosen: close each as explained and carry its text to H18
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch changes only citations and the sentences they sit in, so none of these plan items (the restart as AC-2.3's stand-in and the sign-in after it, the browser's time zone and the next clock-change day, which booking-api@v1 fixtures replay, auth-api@v1 G3 in the AC-2.3 test, timeZone in the proxy replay, the 3-second regression check, a database for each test run) can be addressed here, and the dispatch requires every routed item closed. Each item's citations were read against current text and name current versions (PRD v2, ADR-001, ADR-002, auth-api@v1, booking-api@v1, profile-api@v2); Q-044 names PRD 1 only as the account of what the shipped integration.1 asserts. S11 met the same mechanics for these items and S14 for H16's (DEC-103, DEC-126); the orchestrator kept both. Each carried text keeps the item's text verbatim, so its trail back to S03 to S08 and S11 survives. A way for an item on H18 to wait for H18 would have changed this.

question: How does this citation touch classify against the touched artifact's own versioning rules?

options.label: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
options.consequence: The node keeps its id, Kind, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, phases and every phase section; no contract or ADR file changes, so neither INDEX is regenerated.

options.label: a change for hsdd-reconcile to drain
options.consequence: Would add a Governance updates entry for a Sources move that no contract or consumer can observe.

chosen: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
why: hsdd-spec asks for the classification as one decision. One edit: the header's Sources line, two baseline entries becoming one PRD v2 entry with the sections they pointed at (DEC-130). No sentence was restated, and Kind, Purpose, Owns, Does not own, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, Decomposes into, Isolation strategy, the Overview, the phase table, the dated append and every phase section are byte for byte as before. A node spec has no version of its own. Had a Consumes line needed to change, it would have gone to hsdd-reconcile instead.

question: S15 moved the integration node's Sources line, kept 18 citations, carried seven items to H18 (B-10), and observed without routing that the Overview cites ADR-001 while ADR-001 does not govern the node. Keep the output, and route the ADR-001 observation?

options.label: Keep the output; do not route the observation
options.consequence: The node keeps Governed by [ADR-002]; it reaches ADR-001's restart rule through auth-api@v1 G3, which ADR-001 governs.

options.label: Keep the output; route an adr-update on ADR-001 to add the node
options.consequence: One more step; the node's header would name ADR-001 although it decides nothing about sessions.

chosen: Keep the output; do not route the observation
why: The integration node implements nothing ADR-001 decides; it tests behavior that auth-api@v1 G3 guarantees and that ADR-001 governs on the contract. Citing an ADR as the reason for a contract guarantee does not make the ADR govern the citing node, and the header and affects agree. A phase of the node choosing between session designs would have changed this.
